text: scan_url(url) passes the entry-point parameter `url` directly and unvalidated into _http_get(url), which urlparses it and opens an http.client.HTTPSConnection to whatever host/scheme the caller supplies, then issues conn.request('GET', path_and_query) against it -- a classic SSRF: any caller of scan_url (e.g. a service that lets users submit a model URL to scan) can make the server issue outbound requests to arbitrary hosts/ports (e.g. internal/metadata services), with no allow-list or validation of scheme/host.
evidence: Query: MATCH (c:CpgCall {scan_id:$scan_id}) WHERE c.file_path='src/picklescan/scanner.py' AND c.line>=625 AND c.line<=628 ... -> rows show `scan_url = def scan_url(...)` then `_http_get(url)` (uid 8611ddd710ae66de052eb82eafdd1c4566252afa) at line 628 with zero intervening validation calls. Separately confirmed via EntryPoint query that 'src/picklescan/scanner.py:<module>.scan_url' is an EntryPoint (exposure=reachable, kind=handler), so its parameter `url` is the untrusted source per task convention. _http_get's body (queried via CONTAINS_CALL on method _http_get) shows: urllib.parse.urlparse(url) -> http.client.HTTPSConnection(parsed_url.netloc) -> conn.request('GET', path_and_query) with no scheme/host checks anywhere in the method.

text: _http_get() in src/picklescan/scanner.py — reachable from the public scan_url()/scan_huggingface_model() entry points with an attacker-supplied URL — follows HTTP 302 redirects by recursively calling itself with the raw `Location` header value, with no cap on the number of redirects followed, no allowlist/validation of the redirect destination host/scheme, and no limit on the size of the response body read via `response.read()`. A malicious or compromised server (e.g. a spoofed model-hosting endpoint passed to `scan_url`) can therefore redirect-chain the scanner into internal/private network endpoints (SSRF) or force unbounded memory consumption / recursion via an infinite redirect loop or oversized response — there is no standard 'bounded redirect following + destination validation + response-size cap' control present anywhere in this function or its callers.
evidence: Query: MATCH (m:CpgMethod {scan_id:$scan_id}) WHERE m.name IN ['scan_url','_http_get','scan_huggingface_model'] RETURN m.full_name, m.reachable_from_entry, m.hop_distance -> all three return reachable_from_entry=true, hop_distance=0 (confirmed entry-reachable). Pulled full call sequence of _http_get (scanner.py:250-269): `conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(parsed_url.netloc)` ... `if response.status == 302: return _http_get(response.headers["Location"])` (line 262, no redirect counter/depth argument, no host/scheme check on the Location value) ... `return response.read()` (line 267, unbounded read, no Content-Length/size check). Confirmed scan_url (scanner.py:625-628) passes the raw, caller-supplied `url` straight into `_http_get(url)` with no prior validation. Searched scanner.py for any size/redirect-limit constants ('MAX', 'limit') — only unrelated hits (zipfile magic-byte reads of 1-8 bytes); none applicable to HTTP response size or redirect count. Searched for TLS-disabling patterns ('verify', 'CERT_NONE', 'check_hostname', '_create_unverified_context') across the whole scan — zero matches, so only the redirect-count/destination-validation/response-size controls are missing, not certificate validation.

text: scan_huggingface_model(repo_id, ...) interpolates the entry-point parameter `repo_id` unsanitized into HTTPS URLs (f"https://huggingface.co/api/models/{repo_id}" and f"https://huggingface.co/{repo_id}/resolve/main/{file_name}") that are then fetched via _http_get. Because repo_id is not validated or URL-encoded, a crafted repo_id (containing '/', '..', '#', '?' etc.) can alter the request path/query sent to huggingface.co, and the request still inherits the unbounded redirect-following behavior of _http_get noted above.
evidence: Query: MATCH (m:CpgMethod {scan_id:$scan_id})-[:CONTAINS_CALL]->(c:CpgCall {scan_id:$scan_id}) WHERE m.full_name='src/picklescan/scanner.py:<module>.scan_huggingface_model' ... -> rows show line 578: `_http_get(f"https://huggingface.co/api/models/{repo_id}")` and line 588-589: `url = f"https://huggingface.co/{repo_id}/resolve/main/{file_name}"` then `_http_get(url)`, with no sanitization/encoding of repo_id anywhere in the method body. Confirmed scan_huggingface_model is an EntryPoint (exposure=reachable, kind=handler) via the EntryPoint query, so repo_id is the untrusted source by task convention.

text: RelaxedZipFile.open() in src/picklescan/relaxed_zipfile.py explicitly disables the ZIP CRC-32 integrity check (`zef._expected_crc = None  # Disable CRC validation as PyTorch may not use it`) on every member it opens for reading, with no alternative integrity/consistency check substituted. This class is used by scan_zip_bytes() to read candidate pickle members out of untrusted zip archives (including PyTorch checkpoint files), so a corrupted or deliberately truncated/tampered zip entry that would normally raise zipfile.BadZipFile on CRC mismatch is instead silently accepted and handed to the pickle opcode scanner, removing the only data-integrity check that exists on that path.
evidence: Query: MATCH (c:CpgCall {scan_id:$scan_id}) WHERE c.file_path='src/picklescan/relaxed_zipfile.py' AND (c.code CONTAINS '_expected_crc' OR c.name='ZipExtFile') RETURN ... -> rows: {"zipfile.ZipExtFile(zef_file, mode, zinfo, pwd, True)", line 88}, {"zef._expected_crc", line 91}, {"zef._expected_crc = None", line 91}. Semantic search 'limit extracted file size ... decompression bomb' surfaced the surrounding method body (relaxed_zipfile.py:18-96) confirming RelaxedZipFile subclasses zipfile.ZipFile and this assignment is the only integrity-related statement in open(); scan_zip_bytes (scanner.py:452-468, pulled via direct line-range query) calls `RelaxedZipFile(data, "r")` then `zip.open(file_name, "r")` on attacker-controlled archive bytes, confirming this disabled check sits directly on the untrusted-input path.

text: scan_7z_bytes() in src/picklescan/scanner.py extracts archive member names taken directly from an untrusted 7z file (`archive.getnames()`) to a temp directory via `archive.extract(path=tmpdir, targets=targets)` and then reconstructs the output path with a plain `os.path.join(tmpdir, file_name)` — picklescan's own code performs no path-traversal sanitization (no realpath/commonpath containment check) on `file_name` before using it, and no cap on total extracted size/file count (zip-bomb style) is present anywhere in the function, relying entirely on the third-party py7zr library to enforce path containment and resource limits.
evidence: Pulled full scan_7z_bytes body via CpgCall nodes at scanner.py:428-467: `targets = [f for f in file_names if f.endswith(tuple(_pickle_file_extensions))]` then `archive.extract(path=tmpdir, targets=targets)` then per-target `file_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, file_name)` with only `os.path.isfile(file_path)` as a guard. Query for sanitization helpers: MATCH (c:CpgCall {scan_id:$scan_id}) WHERE c.file_path IN ['src/picklescan/scanner.py',...] AND (c.code CONTAINS '..' OR c.name IN ['startswith','commonpath','realpath','resolve','abspath','normpath']) -> only hit was an unrelated `os.path.abspath(args.path)` in cli.py:58; zero path-containment calls in scanner.py around the 7z-extraction code. No 'MAX'/size-limit constants found in scanner.py via a dedicated search. Confidence is tempered because the installed py7zr version (==0.22.0, per Dependency node) may itself sanitize extraction targets internally, which is outside this graph's visibility.

text: numpy is pinned to a range (>1.24.0,<2.0.0) that excludes numpy 2.x entirely, meaning the project is permanently stuck on the numpy 1.x line (now superseded) for an attack-surface-relevant dependency (scan_numpy() parses untrusted .npy/.npz files from entry point scan_bytes).
